missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Срок' stays in the nominative as the subject of 'закончился'. 'Этот' is the agreeing masculine demonstrative, and 'почти' softens the statement. A natural deadline report.

Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Срок' is the accusative direct object of 'назначил'; for this inanimate masculine noun the form matches the nominative. 'Новый' agrees in gender. Useful for scheduling.
Strategic focus: Genitive modifier. 'Этого срока' is the genitive modifying 'конца'. 'Срока' keeps the full vowel since this stem has no fleeting vowel. A useful possession-within-phrase pattern.
Strategic focus: Dative after preposition. 'К сроку' uses the dative 'сроку' after 'к' to show approach toward a deadline. 'Медленно' adds manner. A natural deadline pattern.
Strategic focus: Instrumental after preposition. 'Перед сроком' uses the instrumental 'сроком' after 'перед' to mean before the deadline. 'Закончили' marks completion. A common workplace pattern.
Strategic focus: Accusative of time. 'В нужный срок' uses the accusative after 'в' to express within a fixed period. 'Нужный' agrees in the masculine accusative. A useful temporal pattern.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'О коротком сроке' uses the prepositional 'сроке' after 'о' to mark the topic. 'Коротком' agrees in the prepositional. Useful for negotiation language.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural. 'Сроки' is the nominative plural subject. 'Жёсткие' is the agreeing plural adjective, and 'сдачи проекта' is a genitive modifier. Good for deadline pressure.
Strategic focus: Accusative plural. 'Сроки' is the accusative plural object of 'соблюдает', identical to the nominative for this inanimate noun. 'Строго' adds manner. A reliability pattern.

missions.phrase: Мы не успели из-за коротких сроков.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Genitive plural. 'Из-за коротких сроков' uses the genitive plural 'сроков' after 'из-за' to mark the cause. 'Коротких' agrees in the genitive plural. A clear causal pattern.
